title: The Blinkless Gamer
briefing: Ravi, 14, plays a strategy game for two hours straight. Afterwards his eyes sting, feel gritty, and then — strangely — start to water. On days he plays soccer outside for two hours instead, his eyes feel fine.
question: Why would staring at a game make his eyes sting — and then water?

clues.title: His sister counts blinks
clues.text: His sister counts his blinks as a joke: about 5 a minute while he's gaming, 16 a minute at dinner. He had no idea.
clues.shows: blinking dropping sharply while he concentrates

clues.title: Gritty and stinging
clues.text: After an hour his eyes feel sandy and sting. They look a little red.
clues.shows: the surface of the eye drying out

clues.title: Then they water
clues.text: When he finally looks away and rubs his eyes, they suddenly fill with tears.
clues.shows: the eye flooding itself with tears to fix the dryness

clues.title: Breaks help
clues.text: His mom makes him look across the room for 20 seconds every 20 minutes. Same game, same screen — but his eyes barely sting.
clues.shows: short breaks letting blinking and tears catch up

hypotheses.text: When he concentrates on the screen he blinks far less, so the thin film of tears on his eyes dries out and they sting; the watering afterwards is the eye catching up.
The light from the screen is burning his eyes.
hypotheses.flaw: Screen light is far too weak to burn — and with breaks he looked at the very same screen just as long and his eyes barely stung.

hypotheses.text: His eyes water because he's upset about losing the game.
hypotheses.flaw: The stinging came first and happened win or lose; breaks fixed it without changing how the game went.
Needing glasses would make things blurry — and it wouldn't get better from looking across the room every 20 minutes.

prediction.prompt: Ravi starts a long game. From the first minute to an hour in, what happens to how many times he blinks each minute?

second.question: And how dry do his eyes get?

concepts.label: concentrating on the screen
concepts.hint: What was he doing that changed his blinking?

concepts.label: the tear film
concepts.hint: What normally keeps the eye's surface wet?

concepts.label: the eye dries out
concepts.hint: What happens to that film without blinks?

concepts.label: breaks let it recover
concepts.hint: What fixed it without changing the game?

transfer.context: Sofia, 15, spends an hour peering into a microscope in biology lab. Afterwards her eyes sting and feel dry.
options: The microscope's light is too bright.
She blinked much less while concentrating, so the tear film on her eyes dried out.
transfer.retryHint: Concentrating hard on one thing for an hour — which of Ravi's clues shows what that does to blinking?
transfer.explanation: It isn't the screen or the microscope itself — it's the concentrating. Focused work cuts blinking to a third or less, and each blink is what spreads fresh tears over the eye. Fewer blinks means a drying, stinging eye.

takeaway: Every blink spreads a fresh layer of tears over your eyes. Concentrating hard makes you blink far less, so the eyes dry and sting — short breaks to look away let blinking and tears catch up.
